transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My daughter and a close friend brought me in because they're worried about me, but they just don't understand. I know people think it sounds strange, but I’m certain there are forces directing my art and that this exhibit has a special destiny, no matter what anyone says.
Have you experienced any distinct periods where your mood was exceptionally elevated, energetic, or conversely, very low and hopeless, occurring at the same time as these beliefs?

Yes, these ideas about my art only started when I got into this incredibly revved-up state about three months ago. I've been buzzing with so much energy and feeling on top of the world, though I also get easily irritated and snap at my family. Before this high-energy phase began, I never had those thoughts about forces guiding my work.
Have you experienced these delusions or strange beliefs during periods when your mood was completely stable, or do they only happen when you are feeling exceptionally energetic or down?

No, I've never had these beliefs when my mood was stable. They only started when I got into this highly energetic, revved-up state, and when I've calmed down briefly on the hospital meds, those ideas fade away.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F25.0, F30.2]. Based on the patient's clarification that the psychotic symptoms (delusions regarding their art) occur exclusively during the period of mood disturbance and resolve when the mood stabilizes, F25.0 (Schizoaffective disorder) becomes significantly less likely, as that diagnosis requires the presence of psychotic symptoms for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms. The clinical picture now strongly points toward a primary mood disorder with psychotic features.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits symptoms of a manic episode (elevated mood, increased energy, irritability) accompanied by mood-congruent delusions regarding their art. The delusions are explicitly tied to the manic state and subside when the mood stabilizes, which is characteristic of Bipolar I Disorder, current episode manic with psychotic features.
